body:
Ran MVP, no crash on my side. Dialog window height does get clamped to 16384, which makes things better. In regards to limiting to a sensible value, it would be difficult to implement nicely, because multi-monitor applications would have trouble spanning multiple screens. The root cause is the smart autowrapping label with no minimum size set. This issue is already documented here: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/83546, https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/80218#issuecomment-1669527304, https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/84662. Setting minimum size on the label fixes the issue.

Original repro:
```
OpenGL API 4.6 (Core Profile) Mesa 26.1.5-arch1.1 - Compatibility - Using Device: Intel - Mesa Intel(R) Graphics (RPL-S)

usable screen: (1920, 1182)
caption combined minimum BEFORE any layout: (1.0, 19185.0)
dialog size AFTER first popup_centered(): (716, 16384) (embedded=false)
native window size from the display server: (716, 16384)
frame 1: dialog size = (716, 16384)
frame 2: dialog size = (716, 16384)
frame 3: dialog size = (716, 16384)
frame 4: dialog size = (716, 16384)
frame 5: dialog size = (716, 16384)
ERROR: Window 2 spawned at invalid position: (602, -7592).
   at: _popup_base (scene/main/window.cpp:2282)
   GDScript backtrace (most recent call first):
       [0] _ready (res://main.gd:62)
dialog size on SECOND popup_centered(): (716, 1182)
EXPECTED: a dialog never asks the display server for a window taller than the screen.
```

With label `custom_minimum_size` set:
```
usable screen: (1920, 1080)
caption combined minimum BEFORE any layout: (700.0, 500.0)
dialog size AFTER first popup_centered(): (716, 569) (embedded=false)
native window size from the display server: (716, 569)
frame 1: dialog size = (716, 569)
frame 2: dialog size = (716, 569)
frame 3: dialog size = (716, 569)
frame 4: dialog size = (716, 569)
frame 5: dialog size = (716, 569)
dialog size on SECOND popup_centered(): (716, 569)
EXPECTED: a dialog never asks the display server for a window taller than the screen.

```
